system.description:
World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 3

The WB has 4 Actions instead of 3. And their first Action becomes uninterruptible.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 4

A deity of the Orbital Heaven Colonies from a tribe of humans that arrived before the humans we know. Lives off of bureaucracy and machinery that orders and terraforms Hingsajagra. Worship grants them Sidhi. Tend to be taller, immaculately beautiful. They have +5 Hale levels and have +2 to all Cultivations.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 5

A deity of the Earthly Cities from a tribe of humans that arrived before the humans we know. Lives off of subordination to the Astrals, after the Heaven-Earth War established the ruling and ruled class. Imagine folk horror gods. They have +3 Hale levels and have +1 to all Cultivations.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 6

An informational echo given flesh by Esoteric Fluctuation. Is endlessly hungry and lost. A spirit. Can dissipate and take on a Subtle Body. Always has a craving that tethers their information to the present world.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 7

+1 on all attacks against Bloody targets.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 8

+2 to all straight argumentation.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 9

+1 to all attempts to gain advantage over someone through wit.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 10

+1 ATK if the target is alone and has no adjacent allies.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 11

+2 to all Checks to maintain integrity.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 12

+1 max Flame.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 13

Corpses made to move again, animated by another force, an Antinomial phenomenon, or by leftover body information. +1 Damage from Holy weapons. Gain +1 max Health.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 14

An Esoteric Fluctuation arising from an imbalance of forces, tainted or ruptured Sidhi flow, or through the intense passion of a cultivating sorceror. Immune to TRAUMA. +1 ATK. +1 ATK against Bloody targets.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 15

+2 to all perception, sensation, and insight Checks.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 16

In Violence, heal 1 after every Action taken. Declare a BANE for this Trait. When wounded by the Bane, lose the healing for a day.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 17

This person holds a lot of power in a local place. He always comes around with at least 2 bodyguards.

World Being Trait · roll 3d6: 18

Upon becoming Bloody, the World Being gains +1 Action per Round instead of 3 for the rest of the fight.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 2

The World Being weeps a lost lover or lost ideal. This is a MIND vs RESOLVE attack against all hostiles in 20m. On-hit: inflict HESITANT.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 3

The World Being is overcome with bloodlust. He beats on his heart and runs his full speed.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 4

The World Being is afeared: she looks for the closest cover and hides behind it.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 5

The World Being seizes someone. VIO Attack against a hostile in 1m. On-hit: target is Restrained as the World Being holds her down.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 6

The World Being feints. Or if she has, she attempts a desperate attack.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 7

The World Being retreats to her allies. Or if no allies, performs a desperate last resort attack.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 8

The World Being attempts to parlay or negotiate with you.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 9

The World Being asks for something. Something physical. Something they need, or are addicted to.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 10

The World Being looks for a sign. Any sign. Or they start scrawling their own sign.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 11

The World Being flees. There’s something she’s looking for.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Gambit · roll 2d6: 12

The World Being starts spouting off batshit insane theory or ideas. Something is going on.

An innate telegraph: a Cultivator with free Actions can respond to it. Most World Beings have d3 Gambits.

Inhabitants · roll d66

The kind of entities and people one can find in a particular locale.

d66Inhabitants
11Adventuring Party. Cobbled together. People from the imperial countries—Ressen-Nalenji, Soreh, and Amatsu. Looking for their shot at fortune.
12Cultists. Those following a local god, deity, devil, machine mind, immortal, alien, or something stranger. Will give their life up for their local god. Will try to convert you into their Cult first. Surprisingly well-adjusted without the cowls.
13Angels. Entities bound to serve a god, a deity, or an immortal up in heaven. Forced to do their dirty work. Usually has a large hierarchy; the angels of each god or immortal are constructed differently.
14Elementals. Spirits that manifest through one of the many elements of the Trichiliocosm. Fire, water, earth, air, lightning, ice, quintessence, space, time, and mind.
15Demons. Malevolent spirits blessed with the ability to scour and possess, to physically maim and endanger. Often loves spreading torment and pain to others. Despite this, they do possess sentience and can reason; they are just predisposed to be seized by wrathful feelings.
16Gods. More powerful entities that can grant favors and power. Possessed with far greater physical prowess and natural Sidhi control.
21Divine Beasts. Animals that have lived for so long due to some twist of Sidhi or Esoteric Anomaly (usually 100 years) that they have begun to cultivate their own Cultivation Womb and have learned how to speak and talk. Greater Divine Beasts are common hunting targets for Cultivators for Divine Beast Cores, which are great items for Cultivation.
22Witches. The ability to wield the natural world into an instrument of will is the precursor to Cultivation. These witches are Cultivators of dangerous arts—specifically of the dark science, engaging in occult ritual and theory to change the world.
23Martial Artists. Not yet supernatural, these are just people that have an appreciation, love, or lifelong experience in practicing the sweet science of martial combat.
24Supernatural Martial Artists. Martial Artists with knowledge of Esoteric Technicks. Commonly knowing Technicks and Magicks that already exist within the Sects.
25Sorcerers. More powerful Magick Cultivators that practice deeper and more dangerous sorceries. Vast rituals that require large stores of Sidhi to perform and cast. Often heralded by various ritual instruments, chantries, and loci made to be used for ritual purposes.
26Alchemists. The practitioners of the natural sciences. Heralded by cauldrons and furnaces. Alchemists transmute the finer and subtler essences of nature.
31Chemists. As opposed to the alchemists' more inframaterial practices, chemists deal strictly with the harder sciences and the physical sciences rather than the dark and akashic sciences. Of course, all physical sciences eventually lead into Sidhi, so even Chemists are particularly well-learned about the intricacies of the Esoteric.
32Medical Professionals. Nurses, doctors, and other medics that help suture and heal.
33Devils. Sentient beings that live as superhuman antitribe against the Deities that mostly live in Orbital Heaven. They are similar in power to the Deities, just with less access to Cultivation due to their forced subterranean living.
34Fishfolk. Fishmen and fishwomen. Said to have been some sort of experiment by some South Sea God. Many can live normal lives, but just as many are easily susceptible to the South Sea God's Call.
35Beastfolk. Humanoid animals. Unlike Divine Beasts (who can look like Beastfolk), the majority of Beastfolk are ancient experiments by old Immortals. One of these Immortals is Mentra, the Mad Moon Mystic and the Immortal of Sorcery. As varied as they are unique.
36Spirits. Esoteric aggregations. This is the most catch-all term for them, meaning this entry can include gods, demons, angels, ghosts, and so on.
41Ghosts. Psychic echoes of the dead. Haunting the living and the places they used to go to. Predisposed to violence due to their confusion and their need to be heard.
42Wizards. It is rare to find a group of wizards. In truth, many wizards are just immortals in another name, or cultivators. Wizards in the northwest do tend to have a more Magick bent than in Shen or Selorong, but otherwise wizard is a moniker for accomplished magick cultivators.
43Goblins. Spirits of mischief and mayhem. Wield weapons and love fighting—death to them is fine as long as it’s from something “fun”.
44Fair Folk. Fairies, elves, sidhe, and other strange creatures of the night. Most common in the Northwest Utter Islands.
45Bidaree. Celestial avian spirit singers of the many heavens. Similar to angels, but are not beholden to a single god, immortal, or pantheon. They tend to the banquet halls of the heavens equally. Possessed of immense beauty.
46Yakka. Earth guardians that were once ogres with long tusks and bulging eyes; they have since become powerful protectors of the Great Law and the Enlightenment Code, dedicated to the Buddhas.
51Dakini. Skydancers who are often in voluptuous womanly form, they are manifestations of violent Enlightenment. Many of those with sufficient Wisdom can see their true nature—those that do not give in to lust.
52Monks. Ascetics who commit to a religious life. Most probably have some level of Cultivation. Most common in the mountains.
53Raxaxa. Malevolent giants that feast upon the bodies and blood of gods. They are insatiable human eaters, cannibals, and shapeshifters. Eolomists believe they are the bodies of humans possessed by demons.
54Asura. Wrathful god-fiends that ally with the Devils time and time again to strike down those in heaven. The gods want nothing but a chance at eternal life and immortality.
55Cultivators. Would-be Cultivators that also want a shot at transcension. They travel down a similar path and thus want similar things.
56Item Spirits. Spirits that arise from items that have existed for long times. Sometimes known as tsukumogami. These items develop consciousnesses and eventually the ability for locomotion through Will.
61Manikins. Robots or machines or even paper dolls that have been magicked to life. Do not have a Soul yet—moved to motion by some inextricable force of magick or esoterica.
62Yenjanists. Followers of Yenja. Committed to the tenets of Yenja, but might be a tad bit too zealous.
63Eolomists. Followers of Eolo. Committed to the tenets of Eolo, but might be a tad bit too zealous.
64Siddha. Those that have great magical accomplishment. A kind of Cultivator that follows the Infinite Code or the Revolutionary Law or the Enlightenment Logic.
65Immortals. Beings that have transcended into at least the Third Realm—the Formless Realm. They are so called Immortals because they will live for long periods of time, not because they are impervious to wound and damage. These Immortals possess great wells of power and technick and magick that they have cultivated over years. Perhaps even centuries. Many others call these wizards and mahasiddha.
66Dialectics. Roll twice and fuse the two together. Perhaps they live together in harmony or in a tense contradictory conflict.

Material · roll 2d6

What materials or resources can be found in a particular place. You can roll this up to two, three, even four times to populate a place with multiple things.

2d6Material
2Raw Resources or Services. Wood, stone, ore, iron. Or even a Place of Power, Hotsprings, Lifesprings (which, when rested in, grants +1 Health healed) and so on.
3Food. Either natural or fabricated. From cup noodles to premium steak.
4Medical Kits or Medicine. Can be used to quicken healing or heal +1 Level during a Rest.
5Miscellany. Cigarettes, washing boards, toys, electronic devices, earphones, and so on. Something you'd find in a convenience store.
6Repair Kits. Kits for repairing and maintaining weapons, items, and armor.
7Ammo. Ammunition for weapons.
8Cultivation Seed. A pill infused with Cultivation Sidhi. Grants 1 XP when consumed.
9Magicite. Perhaps a vein of un-graded Magicite. Can be graded to ensure exchange value.
10Manual. A manuscript or manual for learning how to perform a Magick or Technick.
11Panoply. A weapon or armor.
12Spiritual Treasures. Some sort of weapon, fashion, elixir, or pill.
